slot.brief: Conversion sequence from aniline/nitrobenzene to a target dye intermediate via diazotisation-coupling; identify reagents at each step from options.

stem: Which reagent sequence converts nitrobenzene into 4-hydroxyazobenzene through benzenediazonium chloride?

verdicts.working: Sn/HCl reduces nitrobenzene to aniline; NaOH liberates the aniline. NaNO₂/HCl at 0–5°C forms benzenediazonium chloride, which couples with phenol in cold NaOH to give 4-hydroxyazobenzene.

working:
$\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{NO}_2\xrightarrow{\text{Sn/HCl, then NaOH}}\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{NH}_2$.\n$\text{NaNO}_2/\text{HCl}$ at $0$–$5^\circ\text{C}$ gives benzenediazonium chloride.\nCold alkaline phenol couples at the para position to give 4-hydroxyazobenzene.

Independent check: Sn/HCl reduces nitrobenzene to aniline; NaOH liberates the aniline. NaNO₂/HCl at 0–5°C forms benzenediazonium chloride, which couples with phenol in cold NaOH to give 4-hydroxyazobenzene.
